title: Why You Can't Save Money (It's Not Your Fault... Mostly)
alts: Your Phone Is Designed to Make You Spend. Here's How to Save Anyway
Why Saving Money Feels Impossible (1-Click, Pay Later & Dark Patterns)
line1: Why can't you save money? One-tap buying, pay-later buttons, targeted ads and dark patterns are built to make you spend. Here's how to fight back.
summary: Dave promises to save $200 this month. By Friday his phone has sold him three packages and his savings are at zero. We look at why saving feels so hard: only 63% of adults could cover a $400 surprise with cash and the saving rate is about 3% (Fed SHED, BEA). Then the design behind it: one-click checkout and saved cards remove friction, buy now pay later makes prices look smaller, notifications and $294.6 billion of internet ads target you, the FTC's dark patterns (fake timers, confirmshaming), and present bias in your brain. Finally, why willpower loses and automatic saving wins (37% to 86% in a famous study).
